newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar heads higher, trade supportive.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar heads higher, trade supportive.

text.p: London's August white sugar contract managed to sustain its corrective upturn on Friday as trade buyers moved back into the position and ensured that $320 was again a nearby support point.
Earlier in the week, the market saw a fund-led selling spree which dragged August through support at $320.00 and down to a low of $316.20.
But although trade buyers have been swift to buy at the lows, August still needs to gain another couple of dollars to regain its average value from last week.
"The selling dried up and the trade do need to buy August," said one trader. "I think they've waited too long...and they're having to pay up for it.'
August/October has also seen a similar pattern, widening back out to around $5.00 after sliding below $3.00 at one stage this week.
Technical analysts said the market appeared to have exhausted its downward trend and a test of resistance could be on the cards after the recent upside reversal.
"There is now a good chance that the downmove has run its course," said Adrian Haylor, a technical analyst at Sucden, adding that $325 could now be challenged.
At 1115 GMT August stood $1.10 higher at $320.50 but only moved in a range of 50 cents. October was up 20 cents at $315.40 and volume was a paltry 225 lots.
August was untraded in Paris where volume totalled 200 lots. October was down 50 cents at $315.00.
March dominated volume on Matif's new 100 ICUMSA market, up 20 cents at $293.50.
In fundamental news, Syria has re-tendered to buy 13,000 tonnes of white sugar and 13,000 tonnes of raws for August shipment. The deadline for offers is July 15.
